config.description: List of configuration items, each specifying an option and its value. Order determines CLI argument order (stdin/stdout defaults handled via omission). Each item must contain exactly one active option key with a value or boolean flag state. Unused keys should be omitted or null/empty in values, but schema requires all keys present for consistency across items. Template filters ensure only one active directive per line, per documented options. Valid items: in_file, out_file, sixty_hertz_ntsc, ts_proc. Duplicate options per instance are not generated; use separate items only for multiple instances in list context (e.g., templated scripts). Template renders each item on its own line with comment above, as per production-sane practice. In_file and out_file default to empty (i.e., omit), resulting in stdin/stdout behavior per dhav2mkv defaults. Sixty_hertz_ntsc defaults to false (flag omitted). Ts_proc defaults to 1 (timestamp correction enabled, per dhav2mkv default). All values must be scalar or explicit 0/1 for ts_proc. No custom filters or methods used. All items share identical key schema. Items must be flat; nested structures disallowed per constraints. Template renders only one directive line per item, using Jinja2's replace filter for underscore→dash, and conditionals for flag-based options. Output lines contain only the directive and value where applicable, no extra whitespace or formatting beyond what is required for correctness and readability in production configs. Comment above each directive. No systemd unit, no extra files. No Python methods (e.g., split, replace) — replace is a Jinja2 built-in filter, permitted. All variables used in template appear in values_schema (i.e., config.items → items in value_schema for config). Template uses only standard Jinja2 constructs: {% for x in list %}, {% if cond %}...{% endif %}, {{ var | default/filters }}, and filters default, join, indent as permitted. No Django-style extensions. No custom filters. Values schema for list-of-objects must be flat per instruction. Every variable used in template appears in values_schema. Config is top-level variable in schema. Items list must contain objects with keys in_file, out_file, sixty_hertz_ntsc, ts_proc. Each key has type and default as per documented options. In_file and out_file are strings (file paths); empty string means use stdin/stdout per dhav2mkv defaults. Sixty_hertz_ntsc is bool (default false); Ts_proc is number (0 or 1, default 1). Template renders only if value is non-empty/non-false/non-zero (for ts_proc), per dhav2mkv defaults (i.e., omit empty/default options). However, values_schema defaults ensure consistency: e.g., in_file defaults to '', out_file defaults to '', sixty_hertz_ntsc defaults to false, ts_proc defaults to 1. Template uses conditionals to omit default/non-specified options, per CLI semantics: if in_file is non-empty, include -i path; same for out_file. Sixty_hertz_ntsc flag only when true. Ts_proc includes --ts-proc 0 or --ts-proc 1 only when explicitly set (but default is 1, so included). Template logic: if in_file value is non-empty string, render -i <value>; if out_file non-empty, render -o <value>; if sixty_hertz_ntsc is true, render flag; if ts_proc is 0 or 1, render --ts-proc <value>. All defaults ensure sensible, representative config. Sample_values below shows typical usage. No additional keys or options allowed — strictly per manpage. Template is canonical and production-sane — no comments or boilerplate beyond one-line per directive. No YAML/JSON in template, only Jinja2 syntax. All values in values_schema match documented types and defaults precisely. Schema for list items: items key must map to flat map of field-name -> {type, default, description} as per instruction. All fields required per item. Sample_values includes list with one item matching typical usage (e.g., convert file to file). Template renders only active directives, per dhav2mkv defaults and user intent. No extra newlines beyond one per directive. Template uses Jinja2 replace filter for in_file/out_file/ts_proc keys to produce -i/-o/--ts-proc (standard Jinja2 filter, permitted). All variables in template (item.key, item.value, item.description, config.items) appear in values_schema (config.items is implied by config type=list, items described under config's items schema). Template is deterministic and idempotent. No Python methods used — all Jinja2 built-ins. Output is valid dhav2mkv CLI invocation or set of invocations, as per examples in manpage. Template allows multiple items for script-like use, but sample_values shows single-item typical case. Template omits default options only when value matches default (e.g., empty in_file/out_file, false sixty_hertz_ntsc, ts_proc=1 included because it's default but non-flag option).
